next_mission_recommendation.mission_title: Conductor.py Full Branch Coverage: Process Management and Stage Transition Paths
next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: With conductor.py now exceeding 60% branch coverage, the natural next step is to push toward 85%+ by targeting the remaining uncovered paths. Specifically: (1) Map all process management code paths — subprocess spawning, PID tracking, signal handling (SIGTERM/SIGKILL), and zombie reaping — and add tests that simulate process crashes, clean exits, and timeout kills using subprocess mocking; (2) Cover all stage transition logic including invalid transitions, concurrent transition races, and checkpoint write failures; (3) Add chaos tests that inject failures at each retry attempt boundary to verify the MAX_CLAUDE_RETRIES ceiling is respected under all failure modes; (4) Test the HANDOFF.md write path: context-fill detection, handoff file creation, append-only behavior, and the read-on-startup path; (5) Add mutation testing using mutmut or cosmic-ray to verify that the new tests actually catch real bugs (not just execute lines); (6) Generate a branch coverage heatmap as an artifact showing visually which conductor.py regions remain untested. All tests must live in workspace/execute_mission/tests/ and pass alongside existing suite. Do not modify atlasforge_conductor.py itself.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The conductor.py process management and stage transition code represents the highest-risk, lowest-coverage region of the AtlasForge infrastructure. These paths handle system crashes, restarts, and recovery — exactly the code that matters most when things go wrong in production. Pushing from 60% to 85%+ branch coverage on this code, combined with mutation testing to verify test quality (not just quantity), would dramatically increase confidence in AtlasForge reliability. This builds directly on the foundation laid in this mission without repeating any of the invoke_llm/classify_error/extract_json work already completed.

final_report.summary: Over 2 cycles, this mission extended test coverage for the AtlasForge conductor ecosystem. Cycle 1 audited the invoke_llm() function and achieved 100% branch coverage with 169 new tests covering the new tuple-return signature. Cycle 2 extended coverage to the broader conductor.py error handling ecosystem: classify_error() with all RestartReason enum branches, the retry orchestration loop with MAX_CLAUDE_RETRIES and backoff logic, extract_json_from_response() covering clean JSON, markdown-fenced JSON, malformed JSON, and complete failure paths, and property-based Hypothesis tests for the most critical error handling paths. Coverage analysis identified and prioritized the top-5 uncovered high-risk branches. Final conductor.py branch coverage exceeded the 60% target (up from 24%).

challenges_overcome: Ensuring tuple-return signature compatibility across all invoke_llm() callers
Covering all RestartReason enum branches in classify_error() including edge cases
Testing retry orchestration loop with deterministic backoff behavior in unit test context
Handling malformed JSON paths in extract_json_from_response() without triggering real LLM calls
Identifying and prioritizing the highest-risk uncovered branches from coverage reports
lessons_learned: Property-based tests with Hypothesis are highly effective for enumerating all enum branches without manual case enumeration
Coverage-driven prioritization (top-5 uncovered branches by risk) is more efficient than exhaustive coverage
Mocking at the right granularity is critical: mock external API calls but test real retry and backoff logic
Functional integration tests that exercise real retry loops catch bugs that unit tests with mocks miss
Keeping tests in structured test files by concern (unit, edge, integration) improves maintainability
Snapshot-based audit trails provide valuable context for multi-cycle missions with handoffs
